appBuilderComponents.name: Commerce Integration Starter Kit
appBuilderComponents.description: Adobe's Commerce integration starter kit (App Management generation): scaffolding for bidirectional product, customer, order and stock sync, declared in app.commerce.config.ts and installed into Commerce through the app's own generated install API

appBuilderComponents.name: Custom Integration
appBuilderComponents.description: A minimal custom integration to build out with AI — starts from a working deploy, then grows into whatever your demo needs

appBuilderComponents.name: ERP
appBuilderComponents.description: A stand-in ERP the integration talks to: products, business partners, contract prices and sales orders, every record resettable, with its own screen. Comes with the ERP integration and goes with it.

appBuilderComponents.name: ERP Integration

setupSteps.title: Create the "Confirmed in ERP" order status
setupSteps.why: Without it, an order the ERP confirmed looks the same as one it never saw in the Orders grid.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Settings > Order Status: create erp_confirmed, assign it to Pending (not as default), then pick it for "Order status when the ERP confirms" on the integration's Mapping tab.

setupSteps.title: Give each company that gets its own prices a shared catalog of its own
setupSteps.why: At the cart Commerce tells the integration only the buyer's customer group, so companies sharing a group get the same prices.
setupSteps.where: Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Add Shared Catalog, then Assign Companies.

appBuilderComponents.description: Adobe Commerce and an ERP, on the Commerce integration starter kit: orders get an ERP number, price, stock and order-status changes in the ERP land in Commerce, contract prices apply in the cart, and a screen inside the Commerce Admin shows it all. Comes with its own ERP.
